concepts.def: Meaning IMPLIED but not literally said

walkthroughs.body_html: 'Is the Pope Catholic?' literally asks a question. The implicature is 'obviously yes'.

Cooperative talkers obey four maxims: Quantity, Quality, Relation, Manner.

Break one DELIBERATELY and you 'flout' it — often to imply something.
Deictic words only make sense in context: 'meet me HERE TOMORROW' is meaningless without knowing where and when it's said.

mcqs.q: Saying 'lovely weather' during a downpour FLOUTS the maxim of:
options: Quantity
Quality
Relation
Manner
Tree
Quickly
Tomorrow
Happiness
Text types are arbitrary and have no patterns.
By the word's grammatical function in a sentence — not its meaning. The same word can belong to different classes depending on use (e.g. 'run' as noun or verb).
A noun is always a person, place or thing.
A noun is any word that starts with a capital letter.

mcqs.q: Why do text types have predictable features?
options: Conventions develop because they serve communicative purpose — a recipe needs imperatives because it instructs; a news report needs the inverted pyramid because of how readers scan.
A semantic field is a field of study like physics or biology.

A semantic field is a field of study like physics or biology.
A group of words from a similar area of meaning — e.g. 'whisper, scream, mumble, shout' all belong to the semantic field of vocalisation.
A semantic field is a list of synonyms for one word.
